meta.one_liner: One source of truth for your MCP servers. Write it once, fold it out to every client — secrets never hardcoded, only the tools you need loaded.
meta.north_star: Ship the local-first CLI wedge (schema + adapters + sync/diff/import/doctor + secrets) to an OSS launch, then layer the Cloudflare Pages + self-hosted Supabase cloud on top. Own the neutral mcp.config.jsonc format.
meta.headline_metric: Cut MCP tool-schema context from ~72% to <20% via server + tool curation.
non_goals: Server-side enterprise gateway features (RBAC, org audit, hosted servers) — that is the Composio/MintMCP space, not ours.
Naming the CLI binary `fold` (shadows POSIX fold).
Syncing secret VALUES to the cloud — only config with secret REFERENCES is ever synced.
Implying official MCP endorsement in any copy.

stack.language: TypeScript (strict), Node 20+ for CLI/core, Deno for Supabase edge functions
stack.frontend: React + TypeScript + Vite, deployed to Cloudflare Pages, served from mcpfold.com
stack.backend: Self-hosted Supabase (Postgres + GoTrue + PostgREST + Realtime) on Contabo VPS via Coolify
stack.edge_functions: Supabase Edge Functions (Deno) for auth + push/pull, plus a side Docker service to host/run edge functions independently of the managed runtime when needed
stack.side_docker_service: A standalone containerized Deno service (deployed in Coolify) that runs mcpfold edge/serverless handlers the self-hosted Supabase runtime does not cover, sharing the same JWT/RLS contract
stack.ci: GitHub Actions — lint, typecheck, unit + snapshot + e2e tests, cross-OS matrix (ubuntu/macos/windows), build, changesets release, npm publish
stack.testing: vitest (unit + fixture snapshot), playwright (web e2e), tmp-dir integration for CLI, docker-compose for cloud integration

repo_layout.packages/core: @mcpfold/core — pure, I/O-free engine: zod schema, jsonc parse, secret-ref grammar, profile/tag/scope resolution, drift diff, adapter + provider interfaces + registries. No filesystem or network except through injected adapters/providers.
repo_layout.packages/adapters: @mcpfold/adapters — one small module per client (cursor, claude-desktop, claude-code, vscode, windsurf, zed) implementing ClientAdapter. Fixture-driven.
repo_layout.packages/secrets: @mcpfold/secrets — SecretProvider implementations (env, dotenv, infisical, keychain, op).
repo_layout.packages/proxy: @mcpfold/proxy — local MCP proxy for tool-level curation (tools/list interception).
repo_layout.packages/cli: mcpfold — the CLI binary (init/import/add/sync/diff/doctor/secret/run/login/push/pull), wires core + adapters + secrets + proxy.
repo_layout.packages/schema: Published JSON Schema for mcp.config.jsonc (editor autocomplete) generated from zod.
repo_layout.apps/web: React/TS visual editor + directory + team console, Cloudflare Pages.
repo_layout.services/edge: Deno Supabase edge functions (auth, push, pull) + side Docker service.
repo_layout.supabase: migrations/, seed.sql, RLS policies, config.toml, coolify compose docs.
repo_layout.docs: Format spec, adapter authoring guide, benchmark writeup.
repo_layout.ralph: PROMPT.md (loop driver), PROGRESS.md (append-only iteration log), AGENT_NOTES.md.

conventions.code_style: TypeScript strict; prefer pure functions; no default exports in core; zod-first types (infer from schema, never hand-duplicate).
conventions.core_purity: packages/core must not import node:fs, node:os, or network libs. All I/O flows through injected ClientAdapter / SecretProvider. Enforce with an eslint no-restricted-imports rule and a CI check.
conventions.commits: Conventional Commits. One story per branch: `story/<id>-<slug>`. Reference the story id in the commit body.
conventions.branching: Trunk-based; each story is a short-lived branch merged to main via PR that must pass CI.
conventions.testing_rule: Every story ships tests. Adapters use fixture snapshots (native config in / canonical out and back). No story is `done` until its own acceptance tests pass and the full suite is green.
conventions.error_ux: Validation and doctor errors must name the exact file, key, and fix (e.g. 'VS Code uses root key "servers", not "mcpServers"').
conventions.cross_platform: Every path-resolving function has explicit win32/darwin/linux behavior and tests. Never assume `~` expands.
conventions.security: Secret values never written to git-tracked files. `inline` strategy refuses to run unless target is gitignored, and warns loudly. Pin `@latest` at fold time when `pin` is present.

commands.verify_all: pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm -r build

loop_protocol.description: How a Ralph/Claude loop should consume this file on each iteration. One story per iteration. Never work on a story whose dependencies are not all `done`.
iteration_steps: 1. Read PROGRESS.md tail and this prd.json. Pick the highest-priority story with status `todo` (or `in_progress` you own) whose every dependency id is `done`. Respect `order` as a tiebreak.
2. If no story is eligible, stop and report which stories are blocked and by what.
3. Create/checkout branch `story/<id>-<slug>`. Set the story status to `in_progress` and append a start line to PROGRESS.md.
4. Implement ONLY that story. Touch only files consistent with `files_hint` unless the story genuinely requires more; note any deviation.
5. Write the tests named in `tests` first (or alongside). They must fail before implementation and pass after.
6. Run `verify_all`. Do not proceed until lint, typecheck, tests, and build all pass.
7. Verify every item in `acceptance_criteria` and `definition_of_done` is objectively satisfied. If a criterion is untestable as written, add a test that makes it testable.
8. Commit with a Conventional Commit referencing `<id>`. Open/refresh the PR. When CI is green, set status `done` and append a completion line (id, commit sha, summary, follow-ups) to PROGRESS.md.
9. If blocked (ambiguity, external dependency, failing infra), set status `blocked`, write the reason in PROGRESS.md, and move to the next eligible story rather than guessing.
10. Never mark `done` with a red suite, a skipped acceptance criterion, or a TODO left in shipped code.
global_definition_of_done: Tests added and the full suite green on the CI matrix (ubuntu/macos/windows where the story is platform-relevant).
Typecheck + lint clean; core purity rule not violated.
Public API changes reflected in exported types and the JSON schema if the canonical format changed.
No secret values committed; no unpinned @latest introduced where `pin` semantics apply.

epics.title: Foundation & repo scaffolding
epics.goal: A green monorepo with CI, release tooling, and the Ralph loop harness so every later story lands on solid ground.

epics.title: OSS hygiene & contracts
epics.goal: The things that are cheap on day 1 and expensive to retrofit after adoption: contribution/governance scaffolding, a redaction-safe error+diagnostics layer, schema versioning + migrate, deterministic output, an offline/degraded-mode contract, and a stable --json + exit-code contract. These are foundational contracts later stories must honor.

epics.title: Canonical format — @mcpfold/core schema & resolution
epics.goal: Own mcp.config.jsonc: zod schema, jsonc parsing, secret-ref grammar, profile/tag/scope resolution, drift diff, JSON schema export.

epics.title: Adapter framework & client adapters
epics.goal: One tested module per client that renders canonical → native and parses native → canonical.

epics.title: CLI surface
epics.goal: The wedge: init/import/add/sync/diff/doctor with backups and great error UX, distributed via npx.

epics.title: Secrets
epics.goal: Plaintext tokens never touch disk: provider interface, env/dotenv/infisical/keychain/op, and the three per-adapter strategies incl. the shim launcher.

epics.title: Tool-level curation proxy
epics.goal: The moat: a thin local proxy that trims tools/list to the allow/deny set, plus a published before/after context benchmark.

epics.title: Cloud backend — self-hosted Supabase + edge
epics.goal: Coolify Supabase, versioned append-only config store with RLS, device-code OAuth, push/pull edge functions, side Docker service.

epics.title: Cloud frontend — Cloudflare Pages web app
epics.goal: Visual config editor, profiles, server directory, per-machine sync status, team + audit console at mcpfold.com.

epics.title: Launch, docs, QA & release
epics.goal: Docs site, JSON schema publishing, cross-platform e2e, security review, telemetry opt-in, npm release, awesome-mcp.

epics.title: Security & integrity
epics.goal: Prove the ref-only invariant on every path, treat config as executable code (trust + integrity), redact all output, and harden the self-hosted at-rest + session surfaces. Decision: server-side-at-rest (TLS + volume/DB encryption + RLS); no end-to-end config encryption — the server stays able to read config for the visual editor, directory, and audit-diff.

stories.title: Initialize pnpm monorepo and shared tooling
stories.user_story: As a maintainer, I want a pnpm-workspace monorepo with shared TS, lint, format, and test config so every package is consistent and CI-ready from commit one.
stories.context: Foundational. Sets packages/* and apps/* layout, tsconfig.base, eslint (incl. the core-purity no-restricted-imports rule), prettier, vitest workspace, and a root README.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm-workspace.yaml declares packages/*, apps/*, services/*.
tsconfig.base.json with strict:true, noUncheckedIndexedAccess:true; each package extends it.
eslint + prettier configured at root; `pnpm lint` and `pnpm format:check` run clean on an empty scaffold.
vitest configured as a workspace; `pnpm test` runs (0 tests) green.
A no-restricted-imports eslint rule forbids node:fs/node:os/net-libs inside packages/core.
Root package.json exposes the scripts listed in prd.commands.
tests: A trivial smoke test in packages/core proving vitest + tsconfig resolve.
definition_of_done: verify_all passes on the empty scaffold across the CI matrix.

stories.title: GitHub Actions CI pipeline
stories.user_story: As a maintainer, I want CI that lints, typechecks, tests, and builds on a Windows/macOS/Linux matrix so cross-platform path bugs are caught before merge.
stories.context: Path resolution differs per OS and is central to this product; the matrix is non-negotiable.
acceptance_criteria: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs on push + PR.
Matrix: {ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest} x node 20.
Steps: pnpm install (cached), lint, typecheck, test (with coverage), build.
A separate job asserts core purity (grep/eslint that packages/core has no forbidden imports).
Branch protection docs note CI must be green to merge.
Fails the build on any lint/type/test error.
tests: CI itself is the test; include a deliberately-failing local check to confirm the gate works, then remove.
definition_of_done: A PR shows all matrix jobs green.

stories.title: Ralph loop harness: PROMPT.md, PROGRESS.md, AGENT_NOTES.md
stories.user_story: As an autonomous agent, I want a driver prompt and an append-only progress log so loops are resumable and never redo completed work.
stories.context: Encodes loop_protocol from this PRD into ralph/ so a fresh loop can bootstrap from files alone.
acceptance_criteria: ralph/PROMPT.md instructs the agent to read prd.json + PROGRESS.md, pick the next eligible story, and follow iteration_steps.
ralph/PROGRESS.md exists with a header and append-only convention documented.
ralph/AGENT_NOTES.md captures cross-cutting decisions (path conventions, fixture format).
PROMPT.md references verify_all and the global_definition_of_done.
A README section explains how to run a loop (`while :; do claude -p ralph/PROMPT.md; done` style).
tests: N/A (docs) — a markdown-lint check that files exist and are non-empty.
definition_of_done: A dry-run loop can identify S1.1 as the next story from files alone.

stories.title: Release tooling with Changesets + npm publish workflow
stories.user_story: As a maintainer, I want versioning and an automated publish so `npx mcpfold` reflects merged work without manual release steps.
stories.context: MIT core/CLI to npm; cloud packages private. Set up before first publishable code exists.
acceptance_criteria: Changesets configured; packages/core, packages/adapters, packages/secrets, packages/proxy, packages/cli, packages/schema are publishable; apps/web + services/edge are private.
.github/workflows/release.yml publishes to npm on merge to main when changesets exist, using an NPM_TOKEN secret.
packages/cli declares the `mcpfold` bin and `mcpf` alias bin.
provenance/publint check runs pre-publish.
Dry-run publish succeeds in CI (no actual publish).
tests: publint + arethetypeswrong check in CI.
definition_of_done: A dry-run release job passes.

stories.title: Governance & contribution scaffolding + adapter on-ramp
stories.user_story: As a would-be contributor, I want clear licensing, contribution norms, a private security-disclosure path, and a one-command way to scaffold a new client adapter, so the community can add clients as PRs without friction.
stories.context: The whole spec bets on new clients arriving as community PRs — that only happens if the on-ramp exists from commit one. Retrofitting community norms onto an active repo is disruptive; seeding them is a folder of markdown plus one generator command.
acceptance_criteria: LICENSE (MIT) on core+CLI; a NOTICE clarifying no implied MCP endorsement.
CONTRIBUTING.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, and SECURITY.md with a private disclosure path (mcpfold handles secrets-adjacent config — expect reports).
GitHub issue + PR templates, including an 'adapter request' template.
docs/adapters.md tutorial 'add a new client in one PR' (ties to S8.1) exists as a stub referenced here.
`mcpfold scaffold-adapter <name>` generates a new adapter module + test + fixture skeleton that compiles and is picked up by the registry.
CODEOWNERS routes adapter dirs for review.
tests: scaffold-adapter produces a compiling, registered adapter skeleton in a tmp checkout; required governance files exist.
definition_of_done: A new contributor can scaffold an adapter and open a PR guided entirely by repo files.

stories.title: Error hierarchy + redaction-safe diagnostics (debug mode + bundle)
stories.user_story: As a user filing a bug, I want a verbose debug mode and a 'copy sanitized diagnostic bundle' command that never leaks secrets or ref paths, so I can report issues without exposing my setup.
stories.context: A single typed error hierarchy and a redaction-safe diagnostics layer must exist BEFORE any error-reporting sink (Sentry — which you already run) ships its first event, or ref paths leak into your error tracker. The redaction rule here is the same one S9.3 enforces for CLI output.
acceptance_criteria: A base McpfoldError hierarchy with codes; all thrown errors carry a code + actionable message.
`--debug` / MCPFOLD_DEBUG=1 enables verbose, still-redacted logging.
`mcpfold diagnose` (or `--bundle`) emits a sanitized diagnostic bundle: versions, detected clients, config with secret VALUES and provider ref paths redacted.
A redaction module is shared with S9.3 and, when wired, with any telemetry/Sentry sink (S8.3) so no event can contain a secret or ref path.
Test proves the bundle and debug logs contain no sentinel secret and no ref path.
tests: Bundle/debug output scrubbed of sentinel secret + ref path; each command maps failures to a coded error.
definition_of_done: Diagnostics are useful and provably leak-free before any reporting sink is added.

stories.title: Config schema versioning + `mcpfold migrate`
stories.user_story: As a user, I want my first breaking format change to be a `mcpfold migrate`, not a support fire, so the config format can evolve without stranding anyone.
stories.context: `version: 1` is in the schema but nothing defines what happens at version 2. Ship the migration-runner skeleton BEFORE v1 is widely adopted so the path is proven when you actually need it.
acceptance_criteria: A migration registry maps version N→N+1 transforms; a runner applies them in sequence.
`mcpfold migrate` detects an outdated `version`, backs up, applies migrations, and writes the upgraded config (comments preserved best-effort).
loadConfig detects a newer-than-supported version and errors with a clear 'upgrade mcpfold' message.
A no-op 1→1 identity migration + one worked example (a hypothetical 1→2) prove the pipeline end to end.
Migrations are covered by round-trip tests.
tests: Identity migration no-ops; example 1→2 transforms fixtures; newer-version config errors clearly.
definition_of_done: A format bump ships as a migration, not a breaking change.

stories.title: Deterministic, reproducible output + `--check` mode
stories.user_story: As a user, I want mcpfold's rendered files to be byte-stable given the same input so diffs are clean, snapshot tests don't thrash, and I can gate CI on 'is everything synced'.
stories.context: A determinism invariant every adapter (S2.*) and sync (S3.5) must honor: stable key ordering, consistent indentation, trailing newline. Without it, every diff is noisy from day 1.
acceptance_criteria: A shared serializer guarantees stable key order, fixed indentation, and a trailing newline for all rendered output.
Rendering the same canonical input twice is byte-identical.
`mcpfold sync --check` exits nonzero if on-disk files differ from what would be written (prettier --check style), writing nothing — CI-gateable.
The determinism invariant is documented so adapter authors follow it.
A property/fuzz-style test asserts idempotent, stable serialization across shuffled input.
tests: Double-render byte-equality; --check trips on drift and passes when clean; shuffled-key input yields identical output.
definition_of_done: Output is reproducible and CI can gate on sync freshness.

stories.title: Offline / degraded-mode contract for resolution and sync
stories.user_story: As a user, I want defined, predictable behavior when a secret provider or the network is unavailable, so a flaky Infisical or lost connection produces a clear failure, not a corrupt config.
stories.context: A secrets-resolving, cloud-syncing CLI must define what happens when Infisical is down, the network is gone, or a provider times out. Deciding the contract now shapes the resolver interface (S4.1), which is hard to change once providers depend on it.
acceptance_criteria: A documented contract: provider resolution failures fail closed (no partial/blank secret ever injected), with a specific exit code and message naming the provider + ref.
Configurable per-provider timeouts; a hung provider aborts cleanly rather than blocking indefinitely.
Operations that need no secrets/network (validate, diff of ref-only fields, doctor structural checks) still work fully offline.
Cloud commands (push/pull) degrade to a clear 'offline' error, never a silent no-op.
The resolver interface (consumed by S4.1) reflects this contract from the start.
Tests simulate provider timeout, provider error, and full offline.
tests: Timeout/error/offline each produce the defined exit code + message; offline validate/diff/doctor still succeed.
definition_of_done: Degraded behavior is defined, implemented, and tested before providers proliferate.

stories.title: Stable `--json` output + exit-code contract across all commands
stories.user_story: As someone scripting mcpfold in CI, I want a documented, versioned machine-readable output shape and consistent exit codes on every command, so my pipelines don't break when mcpfold updates.
stories.context: People will script this tool; breaking their pipelines is how OSS CLIs lose trust. Lock the contract before the audience exists. Every command (S3.*, S6.6) must conform.
acceptance_criteria: A documented exit-code convention: 0 = success/clean, 1 = actionable difference (e.g. drift), 2 = error/misuse; applied uniformly.
`--json` is supported on every command with a stable, versioned envelope ({ ok, command, data, warnings, errors }).
The JSON envelope has its own schema + snapshot tests so accidental shape changes fail CI.
Human vs JSON output paths are separated so formatting changes can't alter machine output.
A conformance test iterates all commands asserting they honor the exit-code + envelope contract.
tests: Per-command exit codes + JSON envelope conform; envelope schema snapshot guards against drift.
definition_of_done: The scripting contract is stable, documented, and enforced across every command.

stories.title: Zod canonical schema for mcp.config.jsonc
stories.user_story: As a config author, I want a strict, well-errored schema for version/servers/profiles so invalid configs fail loudly with actionable messages.
stories.context: Mirrors spec §4. Server refine: stdio needs command, http/sse needs url. SecretRef regex ^\$\{[a-z0-9_-]+:.+\}$. Profile client enum of the six clients; scope user/project/workspace; path required for project/workspace.
acceptance_criteria: Config = { version: literal(1), servers: record(Server), profiles: record(Profile) }.
Server supports transport(stdio|http|sse), command, args, url, auth(type bearer|header|none, token:SecretRef, headers), env, pin, tools({mode:allow|deny, list}), tags(default []).
Refine enforces command↔stdio and url↔http/sse with a clear message.
Profile refine requires `path` when scope is project|workspace.
All exported types are z.infer-derived (no hand-duplicated interfaces).
Parsing a valid spec-§4 example passes; each malformed variant returns a specific error.
tests: packages/core/test/schema.test.ts covering valid config + one failing case per rule (missing command, bad secret ref, missing path, bad version).
definition_of_done: Schema exported from @mcpfold/core public API with inferred types.

stories.title: JSONC loader with comment-preserving parse and located errors
stories.user_story: As a config author, I want to keep comments in mcp.config.jsonc and get errors with line/column so editing by hand is pleasant.
stories.context: Use jsonc-parser to tolerate comments/trailing commas. Map zod issues back to source positions where possible.
acceptance_criteria: loadConfig(text) parses JSONC (comments, trailing commas) then validates via the zod schema.
Parse errors report line/column and the offending token.
Validation errors include the JSON path (e.g. servers.github.auth.token) and a fix hint.
Round-trip helper preserves comments when writing back edits that don't touch commented regions (best-effort, documented).
Reading the spec §4 example (with its // comments) succeeds.
tests: JSONC with comments loads; malformed JSONC returns positioned error; invalid-but-parseable returns pathed zod error.
definition_of_done: loadConfig is the single entry point used by all consumers.

stories.title: Secret-reference grammar and parser
stories.user_story: As the engine, I want to parse ${provider:path} references so the secret resolver knows which provider and path to fetch, without resolving values yet.
stories.context: Grammar: ${scheme:path} where scheme in [env,dotenv,infisical,keychain,op] and path is provider-specific (e.g. dev/mcp/GITHUB_PAT). Pure parsing only — resolution is E4.
acceptance_criteria: parseSecretRef(str) → { scheme, path } or null for non-refs.
findSecretRefs(server) enumerates every ref in auth.token, auth.headers, and env.
Unknown scheme yields a validation-time warning surfaced to doctor, not a hard parse crash.
A string that is partly a ref (e.g. 'Bearer ${env:X}') is handled or explicitly disallowed and documented.
No network or fs access in this module.
tests: Valid refs across schemes parse; non-refs return null; enumeration finds refs in nested headers/env.
definition_of_done: Exported from core; consumed by resolver (E4) and doctor (E3).

stories.title: Profile / tag / scope resolution engine
stories.user_story: As the engine, I want to resolve a profile into the concrete set of servers (tag-filtered) with scope/path context so an adapter receives exactly what to render.
stories.context: The 'fold': profiles.include filters servers by tags. Produces ResolvedServer[] carrying name, transport, resolved fields, scope, projectPath, and tools directive. Pure; secrets stay as refs at this stage.
acceptance_criteria: resolveProfile(config, profileName) → ResolvedServer[] containing only servers whose tags intersect profile.include.
Each ResolvedServer carries name, scope, projectPath (from profile.path), and the raw tools directive.
Unknown profile name or a profile referencing a tag no server has → descriptive error/warning.
resolveAll(config) yields the map of every profile → ResolvedServer[] for `sync` without --profile.
Deterministic ordering (stable by server key) for reproducible output.
tests: Spec §4 profiles resolve to expected server subsets; empty-intersection profile flagged.
definition_of_done: ResolvedServer type exported and consumed by the adapter interface.

stories.title: Generate and publish JSON Schema from zod
stories.user_story: As a config author, I want editor autocomplete and inline validation in my mcp.config.jsonc via a $schema URL.
stories.context: packages/schema. Generate JSON Schema from the zod Config and expose it for hosting at mcpfold.com/schema/v1.json. Keep neutral/un-branded in the file itself.
acceptance_criteria: A build step emits mcp.config.schema.json from the zod schema.
A CI check fails if the committed JSON schema drifts from the zod source.
The schema validates the spec §4 example and rejects the malformed variants.
README documents adding "$schema": "https://mcpfold.com/schema/v1.json" to a config.
tests: Generated schema round-trips valid/invalid fixtures; drift check trips on manual edits.
definition_of_done: Schema artifact built in CI and ready to host.

stories.title: Drift-diff engine (canonical rendered vs on-disk)
stories.user_story: As a user, I want to see how each client's actual file differs from what mcpfold would write so I can trust sync and catch manual edits.
stories.context: Engine-level diff that takes a rendered canonical output and an on-disk native file (parsed via adapter) and returns a structured, human-renderable diff. Adapter-agnostic; adapters supply parse().
acceptance_criteria: diffRendered(expected: RenderedFile, actualContents: string, adapter) → structured diff (added/removed/changed servers + field-level changes).
Ignores insignificant formatting (whitespace/key order) — compares semantic config, not bytes.
Reports 'file missing' and 'file present but unmanaged servers found' distinctly.
Output is data (not a string) so CLI can format and web can render it.
Deterministic and pure.
tests: Identical → empty diff; changed token → field change; extra on-disk server → unmanaged flag; missing file → missing.
definition_of_done: Consumed by `mcpfold diff` (S3.6).

stories.title: ClientAdapter interface, registry, and shared shape helpers
stories.user_story: As an adapter author, I want a stable interface plus shared helpers so a new client is one small module with no engine changes.
stories.context: Mirrors spec §5. Interface: id, resolvePath(scope, projectPath), render(ResolvedServer[]) → RenderedFile, parse(contents) → Partial<CanonicalConfig>, secretStrategy. Shared fromMcpServersShape/ toMcpServersShape helpers for the common mcpServers-style clients.
acceptance_criteria: ClientAdapter and RenderedFile types exported (RenderedFile: path, contents, needsRestart).
A registry maps client id → adapter and is the single lookup used by the CLI.
fromMcpServersShape(obj) and a stdio/http entry serializer are shared and unit-tested.
Cross-platform path helpers (expandHome, OS-specific user-profile paths) live here with win32/darwin/linux branches + tests.
secretStrategy is one of inline|native-input|shim.
tests: Shared shape round-trips; path helpers return correct per-OS paths (mock process.platform).
definition_of_done: Registry ready for concrete adapters to self-register.

stories.title: Cursor adapter
stories.user_story: As a Cursor user, I want mcpfold to write ~/.cursor/mcp.json (or .cursor/mcp.json) with root key mcpServers, hot-reload aware.
stories.context: Spec §5 concrete example. secretStrategy shim by default. needsRestart false.
acceptance_criteria: resolvePath: user → ~/.cursor/mcp.json; project → <projectPath>/.cursor/mcp.json (per-OS correct).
render emits { mcpServers: {...} } with stdio→{command,args,env?} and http→{url,headers?}.
parse reads mcpServers back to a canonical partial.
needsRestart=false; secretStrategy='shim'.
Snapshot fixture: canonical → cursor json matches golden file and parses back losslessly.
tests: Render snapshot + parse round-trip against fixtures.
definition_of_done: Registered in the adapter registry.

stories.title: Claude Desktop adapter
stories.user_story: As a Claude Desktop user, I want mcpfold to write the OS-specific claude_desktop_config.json with mcpServers and flag that a restart is needed.
stories.context: User scope only (no project). needsRestart=true. secretStrategy shim.
acceptance_criteria: resolvePath returns the correct claude_desktop_config.json per OS (macOS ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/..., Windows %APPDATA%\Claude\..., Linux ~/.config/Claude/...).
render/parse use the mcpServers shape.
needsRestart=true is surfaced so sync can tell the user.
Fixture snapshot + round-trip pass.
tests: Per-OS path resolution (mocked platform) + render/parse snapshot.
definition_of_done: Registered; restart flag consumed by sync.

stories.title: Claude Code adapter (mcpServers + explicit type)
stories.user_story: As a Claude Code user, I want mcpfold to manage ~/.claude.json (user) and .mcp.json (project) including the explicit type: http|stdio field.
stories.context: Claude Code adds `type`. New session (not app restart) to pick up changes.
acceptance_criteria: resolvePath: user → ~/.claude.json; project → <projectPath>/.mcp.json.
render includes type:'http'|'stdio' per server.
parse tolerates both explicit type and inferred (command vs url).
needsRestart reflects 'new session'.
Fixture snapshot + round-trip pass.
tests: type field emitted; parse handles both forms.
definition_of_done: Registered.

stories.title: VS Code adapter (root key `servers` + `${input:}` secrets)
stories.user_story: As a VS Code user, I want mcpfold to write .vscode/mcp.json (or user profile) with the correct `servers` root key and native ${input:} prompts for tokens.
stories.context: Spec §5. This is the classic silent-failure trap: root key is `servers`, not `mcpServers`. secretStrategy native-input; emit an `inputs` array.
acceptance_criteria: render emits { servers: {...}, inputs: [...] } — never mcpServers.
Tokens are converted to ${input:<id>} entries with matching input prompt definitions.
resolvePath: workspace → <projectPath>/.vscode/mcp.json; user → OS user profile mcp path.
parse reads the `servers` key back to canonical.
A test explicitly asserts the root key is `servers` (regression guard for the trap).
Fixture snapshot + round-trip pass.
tests: Root key assertion; input generation; round-trip.
definition_of_done: Registered; native-input strategy honored by secrets layer.

stories.title: Windsurf adapter (mcp-remote wrapper for authed remotes)
stories.user_story: As a Windsurf user, I want mcpfold to wrap authenticated remote servers in an npx mcp-remote launcher since Windsurf can't do authed remotes natively.
stories.context: Windsurf uses mcpServers but cannot natively call authenticated remote servers; rewrite http+auth servers to a stdio mcp-remote invocation. needsRestart=true.
acceptance_criteria: Plain stdio and unauthenticated servers render normally.
http/sse servers with auth are rewritten to { command:'npx', args:['-y','mcp-remote', url, ...auth headers] } (or documented equivalent).
resolvePath returns the Windsurf settings location per OS.
parse recognizes an mcp-remote wrapper and reverses it to a canonical http server on import.
Fixture snapshot covers a wrapped authed server and a plain stdio server.
tests: Wrapping + un-wrapping round-trip; plain server untouched.
definition_of_done: Registered.

stories.title: Zed adapter (root key `context_servers`)
stories.user_story: As a Zed user, I want mcpfold to write Zed settings with the `context_servers` root key.
stories.context: Zed diverges on the root key. secretStrategy shim; needsRestart=false.
acceptance_criteria: render emits { context_servers: {...} } in the Zed settings shape.
parse reads context_servers back to canonical.
resolvePath returns Zed settings per OS.
A test asserts the root key is context_servers (regression guard).
Fixture snapshot + round-trip pass.
tests: Root key assertion; round-trip.
definition_of_done: Registered — all six adapters now in the registry.

stories.title: Cross-adapter fixture snapshot harness
stories.user_story: As a maintainer, I want a shared fixture harness so every adapter is tested identically and format drift is caught by snapshot regressions.
stories.context: One canonical input fixture folded through all six adapters, each producing a golden output; parse() must reconstruct the canonical subset.
acceptance_criteria: A single canonical fixture drives all adapters via a table-driven test.
Each adapter has a committed golden native file; snapshot mismatch fails CI.
A round-trip invariant test (render → parse → semantically-equal canonical) runs for every adapter.
Updating goldens is a documented, explicit command (no accidental --update in CI).
tests: Table-driven render + round-trip across all adapters.
definition_of_done: All six adapters pass the shared matrix.

stories.title: CLI skeleton: binary, arg parsing, help, mcpf alias
stories.user_story: As a user, I want `npx mcpfold` (and `mcpf`) to run with a clear help surface and subcommand routing.
stories.context: Spec §8 surface. Set up the command framework, global flags (--profile, --dry-run, --json, --cwd), version, and both bins.
acceptance_criteria: `mcpfold --help` lists init/import/add/sync/diff/doctor/secret/run and (stubbed) login/push/pull.
`mcpf` alias behaves identically.
Global flags parsed and threaded: --profile, --dry-run, --json, --cwd.
Unknown command prints help + nonzero exit.
`--version` reflects package version.
tests: CLI integration tests spawn the built bin in a tmp dir and assert help/version/unknown-command.
definition_of_done: `npx .` runs from the built package.

stories.title: `mcpfold init` — scaffold config + detect installed clients
stories.user_story: As a new user, I want `mcpfold init` to create a starter mcp.config.jsonc and detect which clients I have installed so I start productive.
stories.context: Writes a commented starter config (with $schema line) and reports detected clients by probing known config paths.
acceptance_criteria: Creates mcp.config.jsonc with $schema, a sample server, and profiles, only if absent (never clobbers).
Detects installed clients by checking each adapter's resolvePath existence and prints a summary.
Refuses to overwrite an existing config without --force.
--dry-run prints what it would write.
Works in an empty tmp dir and in a repo.
tests: Init in tmp dir creates valid config that loadConfig accepts; re-init without --force is a no-op error.
definition_of_done: Output config passes S1.2 loadConfig.

stories.title: `mcpfold import` — reverse-fold existing client configs
stories.user_story: As a user with scattered configs, I want `mcpfold import` to read my existing client files and merge them into one canonical mcp.config.jsonc in seconds.
stories.context: Spec §8: the zero-friction onboarding path. Parse each detected client via its adapter, merge servers (dedupe by URL/command), and infer tags from which client they came from.
acceptance_criteria: Scans all detected clients, parses each via adapter.parse, and produces a merged canonical config.
Deduplicates identical servers across clients; conflicting definitions are reported for the user to resolve, not silently merged.
Generates initial profiles mapping each source client to an include set.
Detected plaintext tokens are flagged and (optionally, with a prompt) rewritten to ${env:...} placeholders rather than copied verbatim.
--dry-run shows the merge plan; writing respects --force for an existing canonical file.
tests: Import from cursor+vscode fixtures yields one merged config; conflict surfaced; plaintext token flagged.
definition_of_done: Imported config passes loadConfig and re-syncs cleanly (diff empty on the source clients modulo secret strategy).

stories.title: `mcpfold add <name>` — interactive guided server entry
stories.user_story: As a user, I want to paste a URL or npm package and be guided to a valid server entry so I don't hand-write JSON.
stories.context: Interactive prompts detect http URL vs stdio package, ask for auth/tags, and append to the canonical file with a secret reference (never a raw token).
acceptance_criteria: Given a URL → creates an http server; given an npm spec → creates a stdio npx server with optional pin.
Prompts for auth type and stores tokens as ${provider:path} refs, never raw values.
Prompts for tags and updates the config in place, preserving comments where feasible.
Non-interactive flags allow scripted use (--url/--package/--transport/--tag/--token-ref).
Resulting config re-validates.
tests: Scripted add of an http server and a stdio package both produce valid config with ref-only tokens.
definition_of_done: Added entries validate and render across adapters.

stories.title: `mcpfold sync [--profile p]` — fold canonical to client files with backups
stories.user_story: As a user, I want one command to write my canonical config out to every (or one) client, backing up existing files first.
stories.context: The core value loop. Resolves profiles, renders via adapters, backs up existing target files (timestamped), writes atomically, and reports restart-needed clients.
acceptance_criteria: Without --profile, syncs all profiles; with --profile, syncs one.
Backs up any existing target file to <path>.mcpfold.bak.<timestamp> before writing.
Writes atomically (temp file + rename); never leaves a half-written config.
Reports per-client result including needsRestart hints.
--dry-run prints the diff of what would change (uses S1.6) and writes nothing.
At this stage secrets remain unresolved refs unless a strategy is chosen (E4 wires strategies); document current behavior.
tests: Sync into tmp HOME writes expected files + backups; dry-run writes nothing; atomic write leaves no temp on failure.
definition_of_done: Round trip: init → sync → diff shows no drift.

stories.title: `mcpfold diff` — show drift between canonical and on-disk
stories.user_story: As a user, I want to see exactly how my live client configs differ from my canonical source so I trust what sync will do.
stories.context: Uses the S1.6 diff engine; renders a readable colored diff and supports --json for tooling/CI.
acceptance_criteria: Shows per-client added/removed/changed servers and field changes.
Distinguishes unmanaged servers present on disk but absent from canonical.
--json emits the structured diff for CI use.
Exit code nonzero when drift exists (so CI can gate), zero when clean.
Handles missing target files gracefully.
tests: Clean state → exit 0; modified on-disk file → exit nonzero + shown change; --json shape stable.
definition_of_done: Usable as a CI drift gate.

stories.title: `mcpfold doctor` — validate + catch the silent failures
stories.user_story: As a user, I want a health check that catches bad JSON, the VS Code `servers` mistake, hardcoded tokens, and unpinned @latest so I stop losing hours to silent failures.
stories.context: Spec §8 retention hook. Lints canonical config and each on-disk client file for known footguns; each finding names the file, the issue, and the fix.
acceptance_criteria: Validates canonical config and reports pathed errors.
Flags any on-disk VS Code file using mcpServers instead of servers.
Flags plaintext secrets in git-tracked files and any inline token that isn't gitignored.
Flags unpinned @latest stdio servers where a pin is recommended.
Flags unknown secret-ref schemes and missing providers.
Each finding: {severity, file, message, fix}. Exit nonzero on error-severity findings; --json supported.
tests: Each footgun has a fixture that doctor flags with the right fix message; clean config passes.
definition_of_done: Covers every silent-failure class in the spec.

stories.title: SecretProvider interface + resolver pipeline
stories.user_story: As the engine, I want a provider interface and a resolver that turns ${scheme:path} refs into values at fold time, with caching and clear failures.
stories.context: Spec §6. SecretProvider { scheme, resolve(ref) }. A resolver registry selects the provider by scheme and resolves all refs in a ResolvedServer set, memoizing within a run.
acceptance_criteria: SecretProvider interface + a registry keyed by scheme.
resolveSecrets(servers, providers) returns servers with values injected, or a structured error naming the unresolved ref.
Per-run memoization avoids re-fetching the same ref.
Missing provider for a used scheme is a clear, actionable error.
This lives in packages/secrets (may touch env/fs/network per provider) and is injected into core — core stays pure.
tests: Resolve with a fake provider; missing scheme errors; memoization proven by call count.
definition_of_done: Resolver consumed by sync + shim launcher.

stories.title: env and dotenv secret providers (day-1 providers)
stories.user_story: As a user, I want ${env:VAR} and ${dotenv:path/VAR} to resolve from my environment and .env files immediately.
stories.context: Ship first per spec ordering. dotenv provider loads a specified .env without leaking it to the process env globally.
acceptance_criteria: env provider resolves ${env:NAME} from process.env; missing var → clear error.
dotenv provider resolves from a designated .env file with a documented path convention.
Neither writes secret values anywhere.
Registered in the provider registry by default.
tests: Env resolves + errors on missing; dotenv reads a fixture .env.
definition_of_done: `mcpfold sync` can resolve env/dotenv refs end to end.

stories.title: Infisical secret provider (dogfood)
stories.user_story: As the maintainer who already runs Infisical, I want ${infisical:path} to resolve via my existing Infisical setup so I can dogfood on my real servers.
stories.context: Spec §6 example. Parse the path (e.g. dev/mcp/GITHUB_PAT) and fetch via the Infisical client/CLI; support machine identity auth.
acceptance_criteria: ${infisical:env/path/KEY} resolves against a configured Infisical project.
Auth via Infisical machine identity / token from env, documented and never hardcoded.
Clear error when a path/secret is missing or auth fails.
Network calls isolated + mockable for tests.
tests: Mocked Infisical client resolves a path; auth-failure surfaces a clear error.
definition_of_done: Dogfood: maintainer's real config resolves through it.

stories.title: OS keychain secret provider (macOS/Windows/libsecret)
stories.user_story: As a user, I want ${keychain:service/account} to resolve from my OS credential store so tokens live in the platform vault.
stories.context: Per-OS: macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Linux libsecret.
acceptance_criteria: Resolves via the correct backend per OS with a unified ref grammar.
Documented setup command to store a secret (or defer to `mcpfold secret set`).
Graceful, actionable error when the backend is unavailable.
Backend calls mockable for tests.
tests: Mocked per-OS backend resolves; unavailable backend errors clearly.
definition_of_done: Works on all three OSes (mocked in CI, manually verified once).

stories.title: 1Password CLI secret provider
stories.user_story: As a 1Password user, I want ${op:vault/item/field} to resolve via the `op` CLI.
stories.context: Shell out to the `op` CLI (must be installed + signed in). Last in provider order per spec.
acceptance_criteria: Resolves ${op:...} via the op CLI read command.
Detects missing/locked op CLI and gives an actionable message.
No secret values logged.
op invocation mocked for tests.
tests: Mocked op read resolves; missing CLI errors clearly.
definition_of_done: Registered as an optional provider.

stories.title: Per-adapter secret strategies: inline / native-input / shim rendering
stories.user_story: As a user, I want each client to receive secrets the safest way it supports so plaintext tokens ideally never touch disk.
stories.context: Spec §6. native-input → emit client indirection (VS Code ${input:}); shim → rewrite launch to `mcpfold run <name>`; inline → resolve+write but only if target gitignored, with a loud warning.
acceptance_criteria: sync honors each adapter's secretStrategy.
native-input adapters emit the client's own secret indirection and never a raw token.
shim adapters emit { command:'mcpfold', args:['run', name] } instead of the real launch, with no token on disk.
inline strategy resolves + writes the value only when the target file is gitignored; otherwise refuses with a clear error, and always prints a loud warning.
A test proves no raw secret value appears in any rendered file for native-input/shim strategies.
tests: For each strategy, assert the rendered file contents (grep for the secret value must fail on shim/native-input; inline gated on gitignore).
definition_of_done: Secrets never leak to git-tracked files under any strategy.

stories.title: `mcpfold run <name>` — shim launcher (resolve, inject, exec)
stories.user_story: As a client launching a shimmed server, I want `mcpfold run <name>` to resolve the secret at runtime, inject it, and exec the real server so tokens stay off disk.
stories.context: Spec §6/§8. Reads canonical, resolves the named server's secrets via providers, sets env/headers, then execs the real command or proxies the remote. Later also filters tools (E5).
acceptance_criteria: `mcpfold run github` resolves refs, injects them, and execs the real server transparently (stdio passthrough).
For http/sse servers, launches the appropriate remote client/bridge with resolved auth headers.
Nonzero exit + clear message if resolution fails; never prints the secret.
Startup latency is minimal (resolve is memoized/fast).
Signal handling forwards SIGINT/SIGTERM to the child.
tests: run with a fake provider + fake server binary passes stdio through and injects env; failure path errors without leaking.
definition_of_done: A shimmed Cursor entry launches a working server with no token on disk.

stories.title: `mcpfold secret set|test` — wire up and verify providers
stories.user_story: As a user, I want to configure a secret provider and test that a ref resolves before I rely on it.
stories.context: Spec §8. `secret set` stores provider config / (for keychain) stores a value; `secret test <ref>` resolves and reports success without printing the value.
acceptance_criteria: `secret test ${scheme:path}` resolves and prints success/failure (value masked).
`secret set` configures a provider (or stores a keychain value) with the right per-OS/backend behavior.
Never echoes secret values to stdout or logs.
Actionable errors for misconfiguration.
tests: secret test resolves a mocked ref; value never appears in output.
definition_of_done: Users can validate secret setup before sync.

stories.title: mcpfold-proxy core: transparent MCP passthrough (stdio + http)
stories.user_story: As a user, I want a local proxy that sits between a client and a real MCP server and passes JSON-RPC through untouched by default.
stories.context: Spec §7. Foundation for tool curation: correct bidirectional MCP proxying first, filtering second. Opt-in, sequenced last in OSS phase.
acceptance_criteria: Proxies a stdio server: forwards initialize, tools/list, tools/call, notifications in both directions with no semantic change.
Proxies an http/sse server equivalently.
Preserves request ids, capabilities, and errors faithfully.
Clean shutdown + signal forwarding.
Behind an opt-in flag; off by default.
tests: Against a mock MCP server, a full initialize→list→call cycle round-trips identically through the proxy.
definition_of_done: Transparent proxy verified against a real reference MCP server manually once.

stories.title: Tool allow/deny filtering on tools/list
stories.user_story: As a user, I want the proxy to trim tools/list to just my allow-listed (or minus deny-listed) tools so my agent's context isn't bloated.
stories.context: Spec §7. Intercept tools/list responses and filter per the server's `tools` directive; pass tools/call through unchanged (optionally reject calls to filtered tools).
acceptance_criteria: mode:allow returns only listed tools; mode:deny returns all but listed.
tools/call to a filtered-out tool is rejected with a clear MCP error (configurable).
No filtering when no tools directive is present.
Filtering is order-stable and does not corrupt schemas of surviving tools.
A count assertion proves reduction (e.g. 20 tools → 3).
tests: allow + deny fixtures; filtered call rejected; unfiltered passthrough unchanged.
definition_of_done: Filtering correct and lossless for surviving tools.

stories.title: Wire proxy filtering into the shim run path
stories.user_story: As a user, I want tool curation to work with zero extra config: if a server has a `tools` directive, `mcpfold run` filters automatically.
stories.context: Spec §7. The shim already in the launch path also filters tools/list — no separate proxy setup for the user.
acceptance_criteria: When a server has a tools directive, `mcpfold run <name>` routes through the proxy filter automatically.
When absent, run remains a plain passthrough (no proxy overhead).
Behavior identical across stdio and http servers.
End-to-end test: a client launching the shim sees only the allowed tools.
tests: run with tools:allow exposes only the allowed set to a mock client.
definition_of_done: Zero-config tool curation works through the shim.

stories.title: Context-window benchmark harness + writeup
stories.user_story: As a launch, I want a reproducible before/after benchmark showing schema-token reduction so the headline claim is credible.
stories.context: Spec §7 headline. Measure tool-schema token footprint with and without curation across a representative multi-server setup.
acceptance_criteria: A script measures total tools/list schema token count for a fixture server set, unfiltered vs filtered.
Outputs a table and a percentage reduction; reproducible via one command.
docs/benchmark.md explains method + results with the actual numbers.
Token counting method documented (which tokenizer).
tests: Benchmark runs deterministically on fixtures and reports a reduction.
definition_of_done: A publishable before/after number exists.

stories.title: Self-hosted Supabase in Coolify + migration tooling
stories.user_story: As the operator, I want reproducible self-hosted Supabase on the Contabo VPS via Coolify plus a migrations workflow so schema changes are versioned and repeatable.
stories.context: Spec §9 stack. Document the Coolify compose/config, wire supabase CLI migrations, and a local docker-compose for CI integration tests.
acceptance_criteria: supabase/ holds config.toml, a migrations dir, and seed.sql.
A documented Coolify deployment (compose + env) stands up Postgres/GoTrue/PostgREST/Realtime.
`supabase db push`-style migration workflow documented and scripted.
A local docker-compose brings up Supabase for CI integration tests.
Secrets (JWT secret, DB password) sourced from env/Infisical, never committed.
tests: CI spins up the compose and runs migrations to a clean, queryable DB.
definition_of_done: A migration applies cleanly in CI from zero.

stories.title: Database schema + RLS: users, configs (versioned), machines, teams, team_members
stories.user_story: As a multi-tenant SaaS, I want an append-only versioned config store with row-level security so tenants are isolated and history is auditable.
stories.context: Spec §9. configs are append-only (version history like the GradeThread certificate pattern). RLS enforces per-user/per-team access. Secret values never stored — only config with refs.
acceptance_criteria: Tables: users, configs (append-only, versioned, JSONB canonical config with refs only), machines, teams, team_members.
RLS policies isolate rows by owner/team membership; a test proves user A cannot read user B's configs.
A CHECK/trigger enforces configs immutability (insert-new-version, no in-place update).
An audit view surfaces 'who changed the team config, when' from the version history.
A migration test asserts no column can hold a resolved secret value (config stores refs only, documented + enforced by convention/check).
tests: RLS cross-tenant denial; append-only enforcement; audit view returns change history.
definition_of_done: Cross-tenant isolation proven by test.

stories.title: Auth: device-code OAuth edge function
stories.user_story: As a CLI user, I want `mcpfold login` to use device-code OAuth so I authenticate in the browser and the CLI gets a token.
stories.context: Spec §9. Deno edge function issuing/verifying device codes against Supabase GoTrue; returns a session the CLI stores securely.
acceptance_criteria: A device-code start endpoint returns a user code + verification URL.
A poll endpoint exchanges an approved device code for a session token.
Tokens are scoped and expirable; refresh handled or documented.
The CLI stores the token in the OS keychain, not plaintext.
Integration test covers the full device-code round trip against the compose stack.
tests: Device-code start→approve→poll yields a valid session; expired code rejected.
definition_of_done: Round-trip auth works against local Supabase.

stories.title: push/pull sync edge functions (config-only, refs preserved)
stories.user_story: As a user, I want push/pull edge functions that sync my canonical config (with secret references intact) across machines, appending a new version on push.
stories.context: Spec §9. push writes a new append-only config version tied to a machine; pull returns the latest (or a requested version). Server rejects any payload containing resolved secret values.
acceptance_criteria: push validates the payload against the canonical schema and rejects anything that looks like a resolved secret (only ${...} refs allowed in secret positions).
push appends a new version row; never overwrites.
pull returns latest by default, or a specific version.
All endpoints enforce the JWT + RLS from S6.2/S6.3.
Conflict strategy documented (last-write-wins with version history; client can diff).
tests: push appends version; pull returns it; payload with a raw token is rejected; cross-tenant push/pull denied.
definition_of_done: Config round-trips machine→cloud→machine with refs intact and no secret values ever stored.

stories.title: Side Docker service for edge functions in Coolify
stories.user_story: As the operator, I want a standalone Dockerized Deno service running the mcpfold edge handlers so I can host functions Coolify/Supabase's managed runtime doesn't cover, sharing the same JWT/RLS contract.
stories.context: Spec stack: 'a side Docker service to run any needed edge functions'. Same code as services/edge, packaged as its own container, deployed in Coolify, verifying Supabase JWTs and honoring RLS via the service/anon keys appropriately.
acceptance_criteria: A Dockerfile builds a Deno service exposing the same auth/push/pull handlers over HTTP.
It verifies Supabase-issued JWTs and enforces the same access rules (no privilege bypass).
Health check endpoint + graceful shutdown.
Coolify deployment documented with env/secret wiring (no secrets in the image).
An integration test hits the container in CI (docker-compose) for a push/pull cycle.
tests: Container starts, health check passes, authenticated push/pull works, unauthenticated is rejected.
definition_of_done: Side service reaches feature parity with the edge functions and passes CI integration.

stories.title: CLI login / push / pull commands
stories.user_story: As a user, I want `mcpfold login`, `push`, and `pull` so my canonical config syncs across machines from the CLI.
stories.context: Spec §8/§9. login runs device-code OAuth (S6.3) and stores the token in keychain; push/pull call the edge/side service; pull can diff before applying.
acceptance_criteria: `mcpfold login` completes device-code flow and stores the session in the OS keychain.
`mcpfold push` uploads the local canonical config (refs only) as a new version, tagged with this machine.
`mcpfold pull` fetches latest, shows a diff vs local (reusing S1.6), and applies on confirmation (or --yes).
All commands fail clearly when not logged in or when the endpoint is unreachable.
Never uploads resolved secret values (client-side guard mirrors the server guard).
tests: Against a mocked endpoint: login stores token; push sends refs-only; pull diffs + applies; logged-out errors.
definition_of_done: Two-machine sync works end to end against the local stack.

stories.title: Web app scaffold on Cloudflare Pages + Supabase auth
stories.user_story: As a user, I want to log into mcpfold.com and see my account so the web console has a foundation.
stories.context: Spec §9. React + TS + Vite on Cloudflare Pages; Supabase auth (session from GoTrue). Shared canonical types imported from @mcpfold/core.
acceptance_criteria: apps/web builds with Vite and deploys to Cloudflare Pages (documented + a preview deploy in CI).
Supabase auth login/logout works against the self-hosted instance.
Authenticated routes gated; unauthenticated redirected to login.
Reuses @mcpfold/core types (no duplicated config types in the frontend).
Basic responsive shell + theme.
tests: Playwright: login flow and gated route redirect.
definition_of_done: A user can log in on a Pages preview deploy.

stories.title: Visual canonical-config editor
stories.user_story: As a user, I want to edit my mcp.config.jsonc visually — add/edit servers, auth refs, tags — with validation, and push it.
stories.context: Spec §9. Form + JSON views backed by the shared zod schema; edits validate client-side; save pushes a new version. Secret fields accept refs only.
acceptance_criteria: CRUD servers with transport-aware fields (stdio vs http/sse) validated by the shared schema.
Auth/token fields accept ${provider:path} refs only; raw values blocked with guidance.
Live validation surfaces the same errors as the CLI (shared schema).
Save creates a new config version via push (S6.4) and shows version history.
Optimistic UI with error rollback.
tests: Playwright: add a server, invalid token blocked, save creates a version.
definition_of_done: Edits persist as new versions and validate identically to the CLI.

stories.title: Profile management UI
stories.user_story: As a user, I want to create and edit profiles (client + scope + tag include set) visually so I control what folds where.
stories.context: Spec §4/§9. Editor for profiles with client/scope/path/include; previews which servers a profile resolves to (reusing resolve logic).
acceptance_criteria: Create/edit/delete profiles with client, scope, path, include tags.
Live preview lists the servers a profile would resolve to (server-level curation visualization).
Validation mirrors the schema (path required for project/workspace).
Changes persist via push.
tests: Playwright: create a profile, preview resolves the expected servers.
definition_of_done: Profiles editable and their fold preview is correct.

stories.title: Curated server directory
stories.user_story: As a user, I want a browsable directory of known MCP servers so I can add them to my config with one click.
stories.context: Spec §9 monetizable surface (public directory now; private registry later). Directory entries prefill the add flow with transport, url/package, and suggested tools.
acceptance_criteria: Browse/search a seeded directory of MCP servers.
'Add to config' prefills the editor with a valid server entry (token as a ref placeholder).
Directory data is seeded and versioned; adding new entries is a documented process.
Respects the 'no implied endorsement' copy rule.
tests: Playwright: search + add-to-config prefills a valid entry.
definition_of_done: Directory browse + one-click add works.

stories.title: Per-machine sync status dashboard
stories.user_story: As a user with multiple machines, I want to see each machine's last sync, version, and drift so I know everything is consistent.
stories.context: Spec §9. Reads machines + configs history to show which version each machine last pushed/pulled.
acceptance_criteria: Lists registered machines with last-seen, last pushed/pulled version.
Flags machines behind the latest version.
Shows recent version history with author + timestamp.
Data scoped by RLS to the current user/team.
tests: Playwright: dashboard shows machines and highlights an out-of-date one.
definition_of_done: Sync status reflects real push/pull activity.

stories.title: Team console + change-audit trail
stories.user_story: As a team lead, I want shared team configs and an audit trail of who changed what, when, so governance is clear — the paid surface.
stories.context: Spec §9 monetization. Team-shared configs with member management and the append-only audit view ('who added the Stripe server, when').
acceptance_criteria: Create a team, invite/manage members (roles), share a team config.
Audit trail lists every config change with author, timestamp, and a diff.
RLS enforces team-scoped access; non-members cannot read team configs.
Billing gate stub marks this as a paid feature (integration deferred).
Member removal revokes access immediately.
tests: Playwright + RLS: member sees team config, non-member denied, audit shows a change diff.
definition_of_done: Team sharing + audit trail work with enforced access control.

stories.title: Docs site, README, and hosted JSON schema
stories.user_story: As a prospective user, I want clear docs — the format spec, quickstart, adapter authoring guide — and a hosted $schema URL so onboarding is frictionless.
stories.context: Spec §2/§10. Publish the neutral mcp.config.jsonc format spec, the CLI quickstart (init→import→sync loop), and host the generated JSON schema.
acceptance_criteria: docs/ covers: format spec, quickstart, secrets, adapter authoring, benchmark.
README leads with the context-window benchmark, not sync.
The generated JSON schema is hosted at a stable URL and referenced by init's scaffold.
An 'add a new client adapter in one PR' guide exists.
Docs build in CI.
tests: Docs build + link-check pass in CI; schema URL resolves.
definition_of_done: A newcomer can go init→import→sync from docs alone.

stories.title: Cross-platform end-to-end test suite
stories.user_story: As a maintainer, I want e2e tests exercising the real init→import→sync→diff loop in temp dirs on all three OSes so path bugs never ship.
stories.context: Spec §10 format-drift risk. Full CLI lifecycle against fixture client files in isolated tmp HOME dirs, on the CI matrix.
acceptance_criteria: e2e: init → add fixture client files → import → sync → diff (clean) → mutate on-disk → diff (drift) in a tmp HOME.
Runs on ubuntu/macos/windows with correct per-OS paths.
Backups verified created before overwrite.
Secret strategies verified to leave no secret values on disk.
Suite is stable (no flakes) and reasonably fast.
tests: The lifecycle test itself, green on all three OSes.
definition_of_done: Full loop green on the matrix.

stories.title: Security review, telemetry opt-in, and hardening
stories.user_story: As a security-conscious user, I want assurance that mcpfold never leaks secrets, pins supply-chain risk, and only collects telemetry I opt into.
stories.context: Spec §6/§10. Audit secret handling end to end, enforce pin-at-fold, and make any telemetry strictly opt-in with a documented payload.
acceptance_criteria: A documented audit confirms no code path writes a resolved secret to a git-tracked file or logs it.
`pin` rewrites @latest to the pinned version at fold time; a test proves an unpinned @latest is flagged by doctor.
Telemetry (if any) is opt-in only, with a documented, minimal, non-secret payload and an easy opt-out.
Dependency + secret-scanning checks run in CI (e.g. gitleaks + npm audit).
A threat-model note covers the shim launcher and proxy surfaces.
tests: Secret-leak grep test across rendered outputs; doctor flags unpinned; gitleaks clean.
definition_of_done: Security posture documented and enforced in CI.

stories.title: OSS launch: npm publish + awesome-mcp + Show HN readiness
stories.user_story: As the maintainer, I want the v0.x packages published and launch surfaces prepped so I can post and gather traction.
stories.context: Spec §10 launch. Publish MIT core+CLI, submit to awesome-mcp lists, prep Show HN/dev.to/r/mcp with the benchmark headline, and open the WG config-portability thread with running code.
acceptance_criteria: `npx mcpfold` installs and runs the init→import→sync loop from the published package.
Semver + changelog generated via changesets; release notes reference the benchmark.
awesome-mcp PR drafted; Show HN / dev.to draft prepared with the context-window numbers.
A WG discussion thread draft references the shipping reference implementation and neutral format.
Post-install smoke test in CI verifies the published tarball works.
tests: CI installs the packed tarball and runs a smoke lifecycle.
definition_of_done: A real `npx mcpfold` run works from npm; launch collateral ready.

stories.title: Ref-only invariant: suite-wide secret-leak assertion harness
stories.user_story: As a security-conscious maintainer, I want an automated harness that proves no resolved secret value ever lands in a rendered client file, a backup, a temp file, a log line, or a pushed payload, so the core promise is continuously enforced, not just claimed.
stories.context: The single most important control. Seed every test path with a known sentinel secret value (e.g. SENTINEL_TOKEN_deadbeef), exercise sync/run/diff/doctor/push across all adapters and strategies, then assert the sentinel appears in ZERO artifacts except where an explicitly gitignored `inline` target legitimately holds it. Resolution must be memory-only — no cache-to-disk of values, ever.
acceptance_criteria: A shared harness injects a sentinel value via a fake provider and scans all rendered files, backups, temp dirs, stdout/stderr, and push payloads for it.
Passes for env/dotenv/infisical/keychain/op providers and shim + native-input strategies (sentinel must NOT appear).
For `inline`, the sentinel may appear only in the target file AND only when that file is gitignored; the harness asserts both.
A client-side guard rejects a push payload containing any non-ref value in a secret position (mirrors the server guard in S6.4); test proves rejection.
Asserts no resolved value is written to any on-disk cache/temp (resolution is memory-only).
Runs on the CI matrix; a deliberately introduced leak fails the build.
tests: Sentinel-scan across all strategies/providers; inline gated on gitignore; push guard rejects raw value; injected leak fails.
definition_of_done: The ref-only invariant is machine-verified on every relevant path in CI.

stories.title: Config-as-code: trust-on-first-use + version integrity signing
stories.user_story: As a user syncing config across machines, I want any new or changed executable command to require my confirmation and every pushed version to be integrity-verified, so a tampered or malicious synced config cannot silently execute code on my machines.
stories.context: `mcpfold run` execs command/args from the config, and `pull` writes that config from the cloud — a code-execution channel. Combine TOFU (like SSH host keys) with signed versions. Same threat class as the unpinned-stdio-RCE lesson, but via the sync path.
acceptance_criteria: sync/pull detect any new or changed `command`, `args`, or `pin` and require explicit confirmation before those entries become runnable; a local trust store records approved entries.
`--yes` (CI) can pre-approve, and is documented as reducing this protection.
Each pushed config version is signed (HMAC with a per-user key or Ed25519); pull verifies the signature and refuses/warns on mismatch.
A tampered version row (unsigned or bad signature) is rejected by the client.
`pin` may carry an optional integrity hash for the stdio package; a mismatch is flagged.
Trust prompts and signature failures are covered by tests using a mocked endpoint.
tests: Changed command triggers prompt; approved entry runs without re-prompt; bad signature rejected; hash mismatch flagged.
definition_of_done: Cloud-synced config cannot execute new commands without explicit trust, and version integrity is verified.

stories.title: Output redaction + backup hardening for the inline path
stories.user_story: As a user, I want all CLI output and any backup files to never expose a secret, so diagnostics and the inline fallback can't leak what the ref-only design otherwise protects.
stories.context: diff/doctor print file contents and sync backs up prior files (.mcpfold.bak) — both can capture or echo an inlined secret. Redact output and harden backups.
acceptance_criteria: All diff/doctor/log output masks values that resolve through a provider and any high-entropy token-shaped string.
Backups of a file that could contain an inlined secret are created gitignored and chmod 600 (0600) on POSIX, ACL-restricted on Windows — or the backup is refused with a clear message.
`inline` strategy refuses to write unless the target is gitignored AND emits a loud warning (reaffirms S4.6) — regression-tested here.
A redaction unit test proves masked output for each output command.
No secret-shaped string survives in any command's stdout/stderr in the leak harness (ties to S9.1).
tests: diff/doctor mask a token; backup perms/gitignore enforced or refused; inline refusal path.
definition_of_done: No CLI output or backup can expose a secret value.

stories.title: Self-hosted at-rest hardening: volume encryption, encrypted backups, TLS/HSTS
stories.user_story: As the operator of self-hosted Supabase on Contabo, I want documented + verified volume encryption, encrypted DB backups, and enforced TLS so at-rest and in-transit protection match a managed provider's baseline.
stories.context: Self-hosting means YOU own disk encryption — managed Supabase gives it free. Because configs are refs-only, a DB dump leaks topology + ref paths (per the chosen server-side-at-rest model), never secret values; document that explicitly as a design property.
acceptance_criteria: A runbook enables volume/disk encryption (LUKS or equivalent) for the Postgres data volume in the Coolify deployment.
Automated Postgres backups are encrypted at rest and their restore is tested.
TLS is enforced end to end (Pages→edge→DB where applicable); HSTS set on web/API responses.
A documented threat statement: 'DB compromise exposes config metadata (server names, URLs, ref paths), never secret values.'
A verification step (script or checklist) confirms encryption + TLS are actually on, not just configured.
tests: Backup encrypt+restore round-trip test; TLS/HSTS header assertion against the running stack in CI.
definition_of_done: At-rest + in-transit protections verified on the self-hosted stack.

stories.title: Session & device-code hardening + machine revocation
stories.user_story: As a user, I want short-lived rotated sessions, a phishing-resistant device-code flow, and the ability to revoke any machine, so a stolen token or intercepted code has minimal blast radius.
stories.context: Device-code flows are phishable and long-lived tokens are dangerous. Harden the flow from S6.3 and expose revocation in the sync dashboard (S7.5).
acceptance_criteria: Access tokens are short-lived with refresh rotation; refresh reuse is detected and revokes the chain.
Device-code: high-entropy user code, short expiry, poll-endpoint rate limiting, and binding to the requesting machine id.
Per-machine token revocation from the sync dashboard immediately invalidates that machine's sessions.
All sync/auth endpoints enforce JWT + RLS and rate-limit abusive callers.
Tests cover expiry, refresh rotation/reuse-detection, rate-limit, and revocation.
tests: Expired/rotated/reused tokens handled; rate limit trips; revoked machine denied.
definition_of_done: Session + device-code surfaces hardened and revocation works end to end.

stories.title: Web app security headers + dependency/secret scanning gate
stories.user_story: As a user of mcpfold.com, I want standard web hardening (CSP, HSTS, anti-CSRF) and a CI gate that blocks leaked secrets and known-vulnerable dependencies, so the cloud surface meets a baseline OWASP posture.
stories.context: Consolidates web + supply-chain hygiene into an enforced gate (extends the lighter S8.3). Team-invite and share tokens must be high-entropy; access revocation on member removal is already required in S7.6.
acceptance_criteria: apps/web sets CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, and frame protections; anti-CSRF on state-changing requests.
Team-invite / share tokens are high-entropy and single-use/expiring.
CI runs gitleaks + dependency audit (npm audit / OSV) and fails on high-severity findings or any detected secret.
A threat-model doc covers the shim launcher, proxy, and sync channel surfaces.
Header presence asserted by an automated test against the deployed preview.
tests: Header assertions on the running app; CI security gate trips on a planted secret / vulnerable dep.
definition_of_done: Web hardening in place and the security gate enforced in CI.
